sealed.statement: The canonical readiness-planning snapshot has one identity owner: the planning normalizer recognises its own output and returns that same frozen object for a canonical input instead of minting a byte-equal copy. On the seed of a five-node formation, 1430 of 2242 buildPriorityRecoveryPlanningProjection calls per 1000 owner builds were re-normalisations of an already canonical snapshot, every one byte-identical to its input, because every producer (direct build, merge tail, answer paths, the ready-gate helpers and startup-authority) re-normalised snapshots that were already the normalizer's own output; each re-normalisation minted a fresh object and defeated the identity memo that every downstream planning memo keys on. Re-normalisation is a proven byte-identical fixed point, so identity reuse serves nothing a rebuild would not have produced; reuse is gated on the floored planning source generation plus the reference identity of the cluster-incarnation fence, the system-table cache and the membership publication owner, entries live in a WeakMap whose self entry holds no reference to its own key, and every returned object is frozen. Node-scoped memo freshness is unweakened: they still read the live publication component and their miss paths build unconditionally, so a publication move without a table write still mints a fresh identity in exactly one rebuild. Measured on the production-composition rig that matches the live seed within three percent: heavy planning builds fall from 344.8 to 162.4 per second (812 builds per 1000 owner builds, minus 52.9 percent) and gate-snapshot builds fall 22.1 percent, with publications winner reads unchanged at 824 and no new cache, read, scheduler, budget, cadence, window, priority edge or second authority. That the reduction moves the seed's certification snapshot answer inside the 60 second window is NOT claimed here: it requires the five-node GCP run.

Re-normalisation is a byte-identical fixed point, so identity reuse serves nothing a rebuild would not have produced; proven over the publication-state matrix and over the whole production-composition sequence, never asserted.

Identity reuse is gated on the floored planning source generation plus the reference identity of every owner the derivation reads (cluster-incarnation fence, system-table cache, membership publication owner); an entry can never outlive its inputs.

The node-scoped planning memos still read the live publication component and their miss paths build unconditionally, so a publication move without a table write still mints a fresh identity in exactly one rebuild.

No new cache, read, scheduler, budget, cadence, window, priority edge, or second ACTIVE or READY authority; publications winner reads stay at 824 and the drain queue keeps maxConcurrency 1 and maxItemsPerDrain 1 with its macrotask scheduler.
Retention is bounded by construction: entries live in a WeakMap, the self entry holds no reference to its own key so no entry can pin the snapshot it describes, and every returned object is frozen.

The measured heavy planning build rate on the shared production-composition rig falls from 344.8 per second to 162.4 per second and must never regress above 812 builds per 1000 owner builds; the rate is measured on that rig, never projected.

claim: independent landing verification rejected (subagent:identity-owner-review-1): fixed-point-proven: BLOCKING. Re-normalisation is NOT a byte-identical fixed point, and the divergent shape is reachable on release-0.2 formation paths. Shadow-auditing every identity hit across the whole test/control-plane suite (9613 hits, served object vs a forced rebuild of the same input) found 26 hits whose served content differs from the rebuild: publicationStatus null vs 'UNKNOWN', publicationEpoch null vs 0, plus the same two fields and publicationStatusNormalized inside publicationRecoveryGate. All 26 are SELF hits (served === branded input) in formation-release-handoff-closure, formation-release-handoff-consumer-parity and formation-release-handoff-post-reopen-capture, reached through buildPriorityControlPlaneRecoveryProjection -> getPriorityControlPlaneRecoveryState. Instrumenting the SAME three suites at the base commit confirms HEAD serves 'UNKNOWN'/0 on every one of those 26 calls, so the candidate changes owner-visible content on a reachable path. Root cause: the projection spreads its own derived publicationRecoveryGate back into buildPublicationRecoveryGateSnapshot, whose providedPublicationOwnerStream branch defaults an absent status/epoch to UNKNOWN/0 on the second pass; the first pass keeps null. The quest statement, the single-identity-owner rationale and the renormalisation-is-a-byte-identical-fixed-point licence all assert this cannot happen; the licence's publication-state matrix and the rig never construct a snapshot without a status string, so the proof does not cover the shape it licenses. epoch null vs 0 is decision-bearing (isRetainedPublicationEpochAhead branches on Number.isInteger). Repair options: verify the fixed point at adopt time and skip identity reuse when build(P) is not content-equal to P, or restrict reuse to snapshots carrying a string publicationStatus and finite epoch, or fix the gate builder non-idempotence; then extend the matrix with a null-publication shape.; identity-gated-on-inputs: PASS on staleness. No input change was found that alters what a rebuild would produce while a hit is still served. The projection builder reads only its argument plus one live input (the local cluster-incarnation fence), never the system-table cache or the publication owner, so table churn inside the 250ms generation floor, a publication winner advanced without a table write, node readiness changes and counter swaps cannot make a hit stale. An in-place mutation of the fence object (same reference, allowed true -> false) also leaves a forced rebuild content-equal to the served object, because a canonical projection already materialises admissionState, admissionReasonCodes and clusterIncarnationFence. The 9613-hit shadow audit produced zero staleness divergences; the three added owner-reference gates are strictly stronger than the base commit's generation-only gate.; bounded-retention: PASS. Structural inspection of a live entry: the SELF entry is {generation, admissionEvidenceSource, planningSourceCache, membershipPublicationOwner, projection: null} and holds no reference to its own WeakMap key, so no entry can pin the snapshot it describes; the non-self entry is rooted at the input snapshot and references the projection forwards only, so there is no cycle. Returned objects and their publicationRecoveryGate are frozen and a caller redefine attempt throws TypeError, so a caller cannot corrupt a later hit. The entry does retain the long-lived cache, publication owner and fence objects for the key's lifetime, which is bounded and not a leak.; no-new-cache-or-authority: PASS. The diff adds no cache, scheduler, budget, cadence, window, priority edge or second authority: the extra entries go into the existing planningProjectionByInputSnapshot WeakMap and reuse the generation the normalizer already computed. Independently re-measured publications winner reads are exactly 824 on both base and candidate over the shared rig, so read amplification is unchanged and bounded-read-amplification-scope is not weakened. budgets-and-cadence-unchanged (maxConcurrency 1, maxItemsPerDrain 1, macrotask scheduler) passes.; measured-rate-never-regresses: PASS and independently reproduced. Three runs of driveFormationShapedChurn on the candidate: 812 heavy planning builds per 1000 owner builds = 162.4/s, winner reads 824, every run identical. Three runs at the base commit d3e7753: 1724 builds = 344.8/s, winner reads 824. That is exactly the claimed 344.8 -> 162.4/s and -52.9 percent with no rate benefit paid for in reads.; identity-observable-preserved: PASS, and the observable still discriminates. projection-planning-identity-memoization plus the cl-033/cl-034 and readiness planning suites are 356/356 green on the candidate. A deliberate mutation that lets resolveMemoizedPriorityRecoveryPlanningProjectionSync take the identity-reusing path on its miss turns the sealed observable red ('the planning answer memo survives a candidate that proposes the next publication epoch'), so the node-scoped memo's unconditional miss-path build is genuinely load-bearing and unweakened.; candidate-integrity: Manifest verified. Working tree equals the reviewed candidate: git diff HEAD over the nine manifest paths is byte-identical to solve/changes/readiness-planning-snapshot-identity-owner/attempt-1.diff modulo index lines, whose sha256 is the manifest fingerprint c5c5d59488545cbdcc4b00cea8449ce01d1bec6bff8f1df946a3583679b68ce0; HEAD equals baseCommit d3e7753. src scope is exactly the two named control-plane files. Gates: witness 12/12 green on candidate and 6 of 12 red at base (stable-inputs-burst, version-key-change, source-generation-change, identical-counter-cache-swap, canonical-identity-retains-no-back-reference, formation-shaped-build-rate), matching the claimed 6 of 11 receipts. Whole test/control-plane suite 6977 pass / 1 fail, the single failure being no-owner-semantics-change, which is red for any uncommitted source candidate and is not attributed. audit:impact-contracts PASS with digest sha256:894c187f matching the manifest, audit:shards current, eslint clean on all nine paths, audit:guidelines clean, check-guideline-decision-boundaries clean on both changed src files with 11 inherited baseline matches.; brief-deviation-version-key-gate: The implementer's decision to back out full memo-version-key gating in favour of generation plus owner-reference gating is SOUND on staleness grounds and is not what fails here. The publication component is a live winner read taken per projection call rather than per memo read, which is why it cost 824 -> 3066 winner reads for no rate benefit and would have raised the sealed PUBLICATION_WINNER_READ_BOUND of 824; the projection derivation never reads publications, so the weaker gate loses no freshness. Note that the version-key gate would NOT have prevented the blocking finding either, since that divergence is a non-idempotent derivation rather than a stale input.

claim: Verifier rejection on attempt 1 (subagent:identity-owner-review-1), one blocking defect: the fixed-point premise is FALSE in a reachable shape. A shadow audit of every identity hit across test/control-plane (9613 hits, each compared against a forced rebuild of the same input) found 26 divergences, all SELF hits on release-0.2 formation paths (formation-release-handoff-closure, -consumer-parity, -post-reopen-capture) reached via buildPriorityControlPlaneRecoveryProjection -> getPriorityControlPlaneRecoveryState (control-plane-readiness-startup-authority-health.js:414): the candidate serves publicationStatus null and publicationEpoch null where a rebuild — and HEAD, instrumented on the same three suites — produces 'UNKNOWN' and 0, including inside publicationRecoveryGate. So the candidate changes owner-visible content on a release path. Root cause: the projection spreads its own derived publicationRecoveryGate back into buildPublicationRecoveryGateSnapshot, whose providedPublicationOwnerStream branch defaults an absent status/epoch to UNKNOWN/0 on the second pass and null on the first; normalisation is therefore not idempotent for a snapshot without a status string, and the licence matrix (epoch 2/3 x PUBLISHED/ACKNOWLEDGING plus a no-membership-row case) never constructs that shape, so the proof did not cover what it licensed. epoch null versus 0 is decision-bearing (isRetainedPublicationEpochAhead branches on Number.isInteger). Repair: verify the fixed point at adopt time and decline reuse when build(P) is not content-equal to P (or restrict reuse to a string status and a finite epoch), then extend the matrix with a null-publication shape. Everything else passed: zero staleness divergences in 9613 hits (the builder reads only its argument plus the fence, and the three owner-reference gates are strictly stronger than base's generation-only gate), retention clean (self entry holds no reference to its own key, outputs frozen, redefine throws), the brief deviation defensible (the live publication component is read per projection call not per memo read, so gating on it cost 824 to 3066 winner reads for no rate benefit and would have raised a sealed ratchet, and it would not have prevented this defect), sealed constraints intact with winner reads exactly 824 both sides and the identity observable still discriminating, and the rate reproduced exactly over three runs each (812 builds per 1000 owner builds = 162.4/s versus 1724 = 344.8/s).

claim: Sealed doneWhen is unsatisfiable after the verifier-demanded repair, so this Quest is parked for a successor rather than amended: the sealed set requires the receipt source-generation-change-mints-a-fresh-identity, whose claim the repair deliberately changed. Adopt-time fixed-point verification made SELF entries generation-INDEPENDENT (the projection is a pure function of (snapshot, nodeId, fence), so the verification proof cannot expire with the floored generation), replacing that receipt with derived-identity-is-generation-gated and verified-canonical-identity-is-generation-independent. The repair also adds renormalisation-fixed-point-is-not-universal (21600 shapes, 70.5 percent non-idempotent, the cheap precondition unsound), every-adopted-identity-is-verified-over-the-shape-space, shadow-audit-over-the-rig-finds-no-divergence, membership-owner-swap-drops-the-canonical-identity and gate-snapshot-build-rate-does-not-regress: eleven receipts become seventeen and the bar only rises. One amendment (verification-bar-expansion, harness-fidelity) was recorded before this was understood; the honest path for a bar that changes a sealed receipt's CLAIM is a successor quest.

A sealed bar whose CLAIM is falsified cannot be amended into truth; the work continues under readiness-planning-verified-snapshot-identity-owner with the seventeen-receipt bar.
